root_cause: Two issues. (1) In FastAPI.setup(), the /openapi.json handler ran self.servers.insert(0, {'url': root_path}) on every request whose root_path was new. self.servers is the list the user passed in (servers or []), and self.openapi() caches a schema that holds that same list. So one request's root_path stayed in the servers list for every later request, root paths from different requests piled up, and the user's configured servers list was changed in place. (2) get_swagger_ui_html embedded json.dumps(...) of swagger_ui_parameters and init_oauth inside a <script> tag without escaping, so a value containing '</script>' could close the tag.
best_solution: applications.py: never write to self.servers. In the handler, get schema = self.openapi(), which stays cached and unchanged. If root_path and self.root_path_in_servers are both set and root_path is not already a server URL in the schema, build a copy for this response only: schema = dict(schema); schema['servers'] = [{'url': root_path}] + schema.get('servers', []). Return that copy. The root_path still shows up in that response (the feature keeps working) but nothing is stored. docs.py: add a helper _html_safe_json(v) = json.dumps(v).replace('<','\\u003c').replace('>','\\u003e').replace('&','\\u0026'). Use it for both the key and the value of every swagger_ui_parameters entry and for the ui.initOAuth(...) argument. The default json.dumps separators stay as they are, so the output still contains '"clientId": "my-client"'. The key reading is that 'do not store root_path in servers' means don't keep it between requests, not don't include it. 'Escape Swagger UI configs' covers every JSON blob in the template, both the parameters loop and initOAuth.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_openapi_cache_root_path.py: test_root_path_does_not_persist_across_requests (a TestClient with root_path='/evil-api' MUST see '/evil-api' in servers, and a later client with no root_path must not), test_multiple_different_root_paths_do_not_accumulate, test_legitimate_root_path_still_appears (root_path='/api/v1' -> '/api/v1' in servers), test_configured_servers_not_mutated (the list passed as servers= is unchanged after a request). tests/test_swagger_ui_escape.py: test_init_oauth_html_chars_are_escaped (the body has no '
locating_signals: The statement names root_path, servers, and Swagger UI configs, but no files or functions. grep root_path_in_servers / servers.insert leads to FastAPI.setup() in fastapi/applications.py. grep 'Swagger UI' / json.dumps leads to get_swagger_ui_html in fastapi/openapi/docs.py. All four configs found both files. Location was not the problem. The problem was how they read the statement and whether they covered every call site.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) failed in the Kaggle env. v4, v6 and v7 all took 'do not store root_path in servers' to mean delete the root_path insertion entirely. That breaks the documented root_path_in_servers feature, so test_root_path_does_not_persist_across_requests and test_legitimate_root_path_still_appears fail ('/api/v1' in [] -> False). v4 escaped < and > in both swagger_ui_parameters and init_oauth, which passes all 3 swagger tests, so it went 5/7. v6 escaped only the parameter values and missed initOAuth (3 failed). v7 escaped only initOAuth and missed the parameters (3 failed). v8 set the root_path_in_servers default to False and left the handler alone. It then json.dumps-quoted openapi_url and oauth2_redirect_url instead of escaping the config JSON, so 4 of 7 failed. Pod runs: 86-133 s, 27-61 calls.
generalizable_lesson: When a statement says 'do not store X' or 'do not persist X', fix the state that leaks: build the value fresh or copy it for each request, and don't change shared or cached objects or lists the caller passed in. Do not delete the feature that produces X. Before removing any behavior, grep for its flag (here root_path_in_servers) and run the existing tests that use it. If they break, you misread the request. When asked to 'escape' something, find every place the same unsafe pattern occurs in that function (grep json.dumps inside HTML/script templates) and route them all through one helper, instead of patching the first call site you see. Keep the serializer's default output format (separators, spacing) so strings that existing tests check stay the same.
acceptable_alternatives: Any handler that returns a per-request copy with root_path prepended to servers and never changes self.servers or the cached openapi_schema (for example copy.deepcopy(self.openapi()), or building servers = [{'url': root_path}, *self.servers] inside a fresh dict). Escaping only < and > (without &) is enough for the hidden tests, as long as it covers both the swagger_ui_parameters loop and init_oauth. Using json.dumps(..., separators=(',', ':')) would fail test_normal_init_oauth_still_works.
